bug_semantics: With address auto-creation disabled, an authenticated OpenWire client could request a non-durable JMS topic subscription on a nonexistent address while holding the queue-creation and consume permissions sufficient for the subscription but lacking CREATE_ADDRESS/createAddress permission. The 2.53.0 regression test grants CREATE_NON_DURABLE_QUEUE (the advisory prose calls the relevant permission createDurableQueue). The OpenWire topic path created a temporary subscription queue directly; that temporary queue creation also materialized the missing temporary address without the topic path first enforcing the address-existence/CREATE_ADDRESS check. The unauthorized address lived until the OpenWire connection closed.
flaw_origin: The original OpenWire consumer implementation sent topic subscriptions straight from AMQSession.createConsumer into AMQConsumer.init, where the non-durable branch generated a UUID queue name and called coreSession.createQueue(address, subQueueName, selector, true, false). Unlike the queue-destination branch added later, the topic branch never called the broker's auto-create preflight. In the affected implementation this mattered because ServerSessionImpl.createQueue conditioned its CREATE_ADDRESS security check on autoCreateAddresses, while ActiveMQServerImpl.createQueue separately materialized a missing address whenever the QueueConfiguration was temporary. Thus direct temporary queue creation could create its missing address with autoCreateAddresses=false, and the user's non-durable-queue permission reached implicit address creation without the required address permission.
ai_marker: absent — the BIC commit object names author Howard Gao <hgao@redhat.com> and committer Howard Gao <hgao@redhat.com>; its exact message is 'https://issues.jboss.org/browse/HORNETQ-1375 -- OpenWire protocol support'; it has no Co-Authored-By, Generated-with, or other trailers and no bot identity.
evidence: Advisory lifecycle: the Apache reference https://lists.apache.org/thread/4wlrp31ngq2yb54sf4kjb3bl41t4xgtp and GHSA-f4gc-mwrg-q36r describe a nonexistent OpenWire JMS topic, autoCreateAddresses=false, a user allowed to create the non-durable subscription but denied createAddress, unauthorized temporary-address creation, affected Apache ActiveMQ Artemis 2.0.0-2.44.0 and Apache Artemis 2.50.0-2.52.0, and remediation in 2.53.0. Vulnerable path: at tag 2.52.0, artemis-protocols/artemis-openwire-protocol/src/main/java/org/apache/activemq/artemis/core/protocol/openwire/amq/AMQSession.java:createConsumer runs checkAutoCreateQueue only inside openWireDest.isQueue(), then AMQConsumer.java:createTopicSubscription's non-durable branch directly invokes createQueue with durable=false and temporary=true. artemis-server/src/main/java/org/apache/activemq/artemis/core/server/impl/ServerSessionImpl.java:createQueue checks CREATE_NON_DURABLE_QUEUE, but its CREATE_ADDRESS check is conditional on AddressSettings.isAutoCreateAddresses(); checkAutoCreate, by contrast, treats a temporary destination as creatable and calls createAddress, whose implementation always performs CREATE_ADDRESS. Origin search: git blame and git log -S traced the vulnerable non-durable topic createQueue statement through Apache's aggregate sync commit 177e6820b541e0a71b952eebf503a4d2235910c5 ('ACTIVEMQ6-2 Update to HQ master') to the first-party hornetq/hornetq history. The Apache import's AMQConsumer blob 60e1ec283a56932f9adb2273ac28a64fc22a9fde matches the upstream lineage after 770574ca21c98339397b24e86a4a0f0c1ecc87f9, and upstream history shows d0dbe869b803e17785afe6331c024d2fa7fe5d68 ('HORNETQ-1375 -- OpenWire protocol support') first adding AMQSession.java and AMQConsumer.java, including the flawed topic dispatch and temporary createQueue call; d0dbe869 is an ancestor of 770574ca. Parent absence: `git ls-tree -r --name-only 62f4810cde2af914db4549514a8d5ea80d6591ce -- <both OpenWire AMQ paths>` returned no entries, directly proving both mechanism files absent from the BIC parent tree. Fix: https://github.com/apache/artemis/commit/75f51f0198221355e694c4db31e74a268c963cd6 moves a generalized checkAutoCreate call outside the queue-only conditional, uses MULTICAST for topics, and adds JMSTopicSubscriberWithSecurityTest asserting JMSException and no address; the commit is absent from 2.52.0 and an ancestor of 2.53.0. Tag checks resolved 2.0.0=70e319d6e3fbdd8e882d3f791a97050672af8a5a, 2.44.0=437105493d75b6156ba7bb1f77bae93de2182e30, 2.50.0=0ae68ef46e4e12ae251cdebaa047f53b7bb78aff, 2.52.0=1e05c01410ea26e6fe832ededb3683df3ef83645, and 2.53.0=21e513e7d72fa568086aa251461f8ec59f593df4; Apache import 177e6820 is an ancestor of 2.0.0 and 2.50.0, while fix 75f51f01 is not an ancestor of 2.52.0 but is an ancestor of 2.53.0. BIC-only AI evidence: `git cat-file commit d0dbe869b803e17785afe6331c024d2fa7fe5d68` produced only the human author/committer identities and one-line issue message quoted in ai_marker, with no trailers.
reasoning: The vulnerable capability is not merely that a temporary queue was created; it is that creating an OpenWire non-durable topic subscription on a missing address reached implicit temporary-address creation without the authorization preflight required for that address. The 2.53.0 fix identifies the missing boundary exactly: AMQSession previously checked auto-creation only for queue destinations, while AMQConsumer's topic branch performed direct queue creation. The smallest source commit that first wrote both the unchecked topic handoff and the non-durable temporary createQueue operation is upstream HornetQ commit d0dbe869b803e17785afe6331c024d2fa7fe5d68. Apache commit 177e6820b541e0a71b952eebf503a4d2235910c5 is a large 'Update to HQ master' aggregate importing an already-existing implementation, so treating it as the BIC would violate the aggregate-import rule; matching blob lineage and the upstream file history make the decomposition reconstructable. The direct parent 62f4810cde2af914db4549514a8d5ea80d6591ce has neither OpenWire AMQ file, establishing immediate-parent absence. The imported mechanism precedes the first affected 2.0.0 tag and remains before the renamed-package 2.50.0 boundary; direct fix 75f51f0198221355e694c4db31e74a268c963cd6 lands only in the 2.53.0 patched boundary. Finally, the d0dbe869 commit object contains only Howard Gao's human identity and no AI authorship/co-authorship marker, so under BIC-only attribution the closed verdict is NOT_AI regardless of any later development context.
